name: Unit tests

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

# A newer push to the same pull request or to main makes the running tests
# pointless, so they are cancelled.
concurrency:
  group: test-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # make test (the self-tests of scripts/scrub-key and scripts/vpn-routes,
  # the Go tests and the app's JVM unit tests) and make lint (Android lint,
  # failing on errors only). Neither needs a device, a network key or a
  # secret, so this job finishes long before the emulator jobs and is the
  # first to show a broken change.
  test:
    name: Unit tests and lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      # The Makefile's own SDK in binaries/, as in the preview job: the
      # runner's SDK lacks the NDK version the Makefile needs.
      ANDROID_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/android-sdk
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: golib/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: golib/go.sum

      # The JDK, Android SDK and NDK, Gradle and gomobile that the Makefile
      # downloads into binaries/, under the same key as the preview job, so
      # the two share one cache entry.
      # The JDK, Android SDK and NDK, Gradle and gomobile that the Makefile
      # downloads into binaries/. Every workflow caches them with the same
      # paths and key, so GitHub stores them once per branch instead of once
      # per workflow. GitHub keeps at most 10 GB of caches per repository and
      # drops the oldest beyond that, and this bundle is about 1.2 GB. The
      # emulator, its system image and the test peer's files are left out;
      # the E2E and network jobs cache them under keys of their own.
      - name: Cache the build tools
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries
            !binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            !binaries/android-sdk/system-images
            !binaries/testpeer
          key: build-tools-${{ hashFiles('Makefile', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      - name: Run the unit tests
        run: make test

      - name: Run lint
        run: make lint

      - name: Upload the test and lint reports
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: unit-test-reports
          path: |
            app/build/reports/tests/
            app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.*
          if-no-files-found: ignore

name: Cache cleanup

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]

# Caches saved by a pull request's runs belong to its merge ref, which
# nothing reads once the pull request is closed. GitHub keeps them for a
# week and counts them against the repository's 10 GB, so they push out the
# caches of main and of open pull requests. This deletes them as soon as the
# pull request is closed or merged.
jobs:
  cleanup:
    name: Delete the pull request's caches
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - name: Delete the caches of this pull request's merge ref
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          REF: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
        run: |
          ids=$(gh cache list --ref "$REF" --limit 100 --json id --jq '.[].id')
          for id in $ids; do
            gh cache delete "$id"
          done
          echo "deleted $(echo "$ids" | grep -c . || true) caches of $REF"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs the Android emulator and the API 35 x86_64 system image into the
# Makefile's SDK (binaries/android-sdk) for the CI jobs, retrying a broken
# download.
#
# sdkmanager prints "An error occurred while preparing SDK package" for a
# corrupt download and still exits 0, so success is decided by the files
# being there, not by its exit code.
set -euo pipefail

ANDROID_HOME="${ANDROID_HOME:?ANDROID_HOME must point at the SDK}"
SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
IMAGE="system-images;android-35;default;x86_64"
IMAGE_DIR="$ANDROID_HOME/system-images/android-35/default/x86_64"
ATTEMPTS=3

installed() {
    [ -x "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" ] && [ -f "$IMAGE_DIR/system.img" ]
}

[ -x "$SDKMANAGER" ] || { echo "no sdkmanager at $SDKMANAGER (run make e2e-build first)" >&2; exit 1; }
yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

for attempt in $(seq "$ATTEMPTS"); do
    "$SDKMANAGER" --install emulator "$IMAGE" || true
    if installed; then
        echo "emulator and system image installed (attempt $attempt)"
        exit 0
    fi
    echo "attempt $attempt of $ATTEMPTS did not leave a usable emulator and system image" >&2
    rm -rf "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator" "$IMAGE_DIR"
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ]; then sleep 10; fi
done

echo "could not install the emulator and system image after $ATTEMPTS attempts" >&2
exit 1

name: Network tests

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

# A newer push to the same pull request or to main makes the running tests
# pointless, so they are cancelled.
concurrency:
  group: network-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # make network-test: the debug app on an Android emulator joins the network
  # of a QEMU VM running edgevpn (scripts/testpeer), pings it both ways, turns
  # off for longer than the VM's 60 second ownership TTL and checks that
  # traffic comes back after turning on again. The network key is a
  # temporary one the VM generates for the run, so the job needs no secret.
  # make network-test-address-in-use then moves the VM to the app's address
  # and checks that the app warns about it.
  network:
    name: Network tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      # One SDK and one adb for the build, the emulator runner and the test,
      # as in the E2E tests job.
      ANDROID_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/android-sdk
      ANDROID_SDK_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/android-sdk
      JAVA_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/jdk-17
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # The emulator refuses to start when the runner has less free disk than
      # its userdata partition needs. The runner image ships toolchains this
      # job never touches: it builds with its own Android SDK, JDK and Go under
      # binaries/ and the Go setup action, and runs no containers. Deleting
      # them frees several GB before the caches are restored into the space.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL /usr/local/share/boost
          sudo docker image prune --all --force
          df -h /

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: golib/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: golib/go.sum

      - name: Install QEMU and xorriso
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends qemu-system-x86 qemu-utils xorriso

      # Every cache below is restored here and saved by its own step as soon
      # as its contents are ready, so a failed test still leaves them for the
      # next run. A pull request can only read caches saved by its own runs
      # or by main, so a cache lost on main means a slow first run on every
      # new pull request. The E2E tests job explains the same layout.

      # The same tools cache as every other workflow (see the unit tests
      # job). The test peer's files are cached below under a key of their
      # own.
      - name: Restore the build tools
        id: tools-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries
            !binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            !binaries/android-sdk/system-images
            !binaries/testpeer
          key: build-tools-${{ hashFiles('Makefile', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      - name: Restore the emulator and system image
        id: emulator-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            binaries/android-sdk/system-images/android-35/default/x86_64
          key: android-sdk-emulator-35-default-x86_64

      - name: Restore the device and its snapshot
        id: avd-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.android/avd/*
            ~/.android/adb*
          key: android-avd-35-default-x86_64-disk2g-pixel6-clean

      # The emulator writes lock files into the device directory that hold
      # its process ID, such as snapshot.lock.lock, and can leave them behind
      # when it is killed, so the cached device carries them. On a new runner
      # the emulator treats a lock as held when any live process has that ID,
      # and exits with "A snapshot operation for 'test' is pending and timeout
      # has expired". Nothing runs the device at this point, so every lock in
      # it is stale.
      - name: Remove stale emulator locks from the cached device
        run: if [ -d ~/.android/avd ]; then find ~/.android/avd -name '*.lock' -type f -print -delete; fi

      # The Debian cloud image and the edgevpn binary built for the VM. The
      # script names both by version, and the key changes with the script
      # (which pins the image) and with go.mod (which pins edgevpn).
      - name: Restore the test peer's image and edgevpn
        id: testpeer-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries/testpeer/*.qcow2
            binaries/testpeer/edgevpn-*
          key: testpeer-${{ hashFiles('scripts/testpeer', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      - name: Build the app and the tests
        run: make e2e-build

      - name: Save the build tools
        if: steps.tools-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries
            !binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            !binaries/android-sdk/system-images
            !binaries/testpeer
          key: build-tools-${{ hashFiles('Makefile', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      # Installed here rather than left to the emulator runner; see the E2E
      # tests job.
      - name: Install the emulator and system image, only when not cached
        if: steps.emulator-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: scripts/ci-install-emulator

      - name: Save the emulator and system image
        if: steps.emulator-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            binaries/android-sdk/system-images/android-35/default/x86_64
          key: android-sdk-emulator-35-default-x86_64

      # The emulator and the VM both need hardware acceleration, and the
      # runner ships /dev/kvm owned by a group the job's user is not in.
      - name: Let this job use KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' \
            | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm

      # Started before the emulator, so a VM that cannot boot fails the job
      # early and on its own.
      - name: Start the test peer
        run: make peer-up

      - name: Save the test peer's image and edgevpn
        if: steps.testpeer-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries/testpeer/*.qcow2
            binaries/testpeer/edgevpn-*
          key: testpeer-${{ hashFiles('scripts/testpeer', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      - name: Create the device, only when it is not cached
        if: steps.avd-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 35
          target: default
          arch: x86_64
          force-avd-creation: false
          # A small userdata partition, so the AVD fits in what the runner has
          # left. The create step and the run step must agree, because they
          # share one cached AVD.
          disk-size: 2048M
          profile: pixel_6
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -camera-back none
          disable-animations: false
          script: echo "Device created and snapshotted for the cache."

      - name: Remove emulator locks before caching the device
        if: steps.avd-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: if [ -d ~/.android/avd ]; then find ~/.android/avd -name '*.lock' -type f -print -delete; fi

      - name: Save the device and its snapshot
        if: steps.avd-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.android/avd/*
            ~/.android/adb*
          key: android-avd-35-default-x86_64-disk2g-pixel6-clean

      # The runner's emulator is emulator-5554.
      - name: Run the network test
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 35
          target: default
          arch: x86_64
          force-avd-creation: false
          # A small userdata partition, so the AVD fits in what the runner has
          # left. The create step and the run step must agree, because they
          # share one cached AVD.
          disk-size: 2048M
          profile: pixel_6
          emulator-options: -no-snapshot-save -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -camera-back none
          disable-animations: true
          # The basic check, then the address-in-use check against the same
          # peer, in one emulator boot.
          script: make network-test ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554 && make network-test-address-in-use ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554

      # The VM's console log, which also covers a VM that never came up and
      # so never reached the test. The script replaces the key in it.
      - name: Show the VM's console log
        if: failure()
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/network-test
          scripts/testpeer serial > build/network-test/testpeer-serial.log || true
          tail -n 60 build/network-test/testpeer-serial.log

      # The app's log, the VM's edgevpn and console logs and the screenshots.
      # The logs have the key replaced with a placeholder wherever it shows
      # up. The screenshots are not scrubbed; they show only the app's
      # screens for this run's throwaway key.
      - name: Upload the logs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: network-test-logs
          path: build/network-test/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Stop the test peer
        if: always()
        run: make peer-down

name: E2E tests

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

# A newer push to the same pull request or to main makes the running tests
# pointless, so they are cancelled.
concurrency:
  group: e2e-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # The screen tests in app/src/androidTest, run on an Android emulator. They
  # drive the real screens with a chosen network snapshot instead of a
  # running node, so the job needs no network key and no secret. Joining a
  # real network is checked by hand on a local emulator, never here.
  e2e:
    name: E2E tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      # The Makefile's own SDK in binaries/, as in the preview job, and the
      # emulator is installed into the same SDK. That way there is one adb:
      # the emulator runner starts the device with it and Gradle talks to the
      # device with it. A second adb of another version would restart the adb
      # server and drop the device in the middle of the run.
      ANDROID_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/android-sdk
      ANDROID_SDK_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/android-sdk
      # The JDK the Makefile downloads, so the emulator runner's sdkmanager
      # and avdmanager run on the same Java as the build.
      JAVA_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/jdk-17
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # The emulator refuses to start when the runner has less free disk than
      # its userdata partition needs. The runner image ships toolchains this
      # job never touches: it builds with its own Android SDK, JDK and Go under
      # binaries/ and the Go setup action, and runs no containers. Deleting
      # them frees several GB before the caches are restored into the space.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL /usr/local/share/boost
          sudo docker image prune --all --force
          df -h /

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: golib/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: golib/go.sum

      # Every cache below is restored here and saved by its own step as soon
      # as its contents are ready, instead of at the end of the job. A cache
      # saved at the end is lost when the tests fail, and a pull request can
      # only read caches saved by its own runs or by main. With end-of-job
      # saving, one failed run on main left every new pull request to
      # download and build everything again.

      # The JDK, Android SDK and NDK, Gradle and gomobile that the Makefile
      # downloads into binaries/, under the cache every workflow shares (see
      # the unit tests job). The emulator and its system image live in the
      # same SDK but are left out, because the next cache holds them under a
      # key of their own.
      - name: Restore the build tools
        id: tools-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries
            !binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            !binaries/android-sdk/system-images
            !binaries/testpeer
          key: build-tools-${{ hashFiles('Makefile', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      # The system image is about 1.7GB and the emulator another 800MB, the
      # same bytes on every run. The key names the exact image, so a change
      # of API level or architecture fetches once and then caches again under
      # its own key instead of silently reusing the wrong one.
      - name: Restore the emulator and system image
        id: emulator-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            binaries/android-sdk/system-images/android-35/default/x86_64
          key: android-sdk-emulator-35-default-x86_64

      # The device itself, and the snapshot it boots from. Creating it and
      # waiting for a first cold boot takes a couple of minutes; restoring
      # this makes later runs start in seconds.
      - name: Restore the device and its snapshot
        id: avd-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.android/avd/*
            ~/.android/adb*
          key: android-avd-35-default-x86_64-disk2g-pixel6-clean

      # The emulator writes lock files into the device directory that hold
      # its process ID, such as snapshot.lock.lock, and can leave them behind
      # when it is killed, so the cached device carries them. On a new runner
      # the emulator treats a lock as held when any live process has that ID,
      # and exits with "A snapshot operation for 'test' is pending and timeout
      # has expired". Nothing runs the device at this point, so every lock in
      # it is stale.
      - name: Remove stale emulator locks from the cached device
        run: if [ -d ~/.android/avd ]; then find ~/.android/avd -name '*.lock' -type f -print -delete; fi

      # The slow part, done before an emulator is running: the Go library for
      # the phone and the x86_64 emulator, the app and the test APK. This
      # also installs the SDK that the emulator runner below needs.
      - name: Build the app and the tests
        run: make e2e-build

      - name: Save the build tools
        if: steps.tools-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries
            !binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            !binaries/android-sdk/system-images
            !binaries/testpeer
          key: build-tools-${{ hashFiles('Makefile', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      # Installed here rather than left to the emulator runner, which reports
      # a broken download only as a warning and then fails later with an
      # unrelated adb error. Here a download is retried and checked.
      - name: Install the emulator and system image, only when not cached
        if: steps.emulator-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: scripts/ci-install-emulator

      - name: Save the emulator and system image
        if: steps.emulator-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            binaries/android-sdk/system-images/android-35/default/x86_64
          key: android-sdk-emulator-35-default-x86_64

      # The emulator needs hardware acceleration to be usable, and the runner
      # ships /dev/kvm owned by a group the job's user is not in. This rule
      # opens it; without it the emulator falls back to software and the job
      # takes too long to be worth running.
      - name: Let this job use KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' \
            | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm

      - name: Create the device, only when it is not cached
        if: steps.avd-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 35
          target: default
          arch: x86_64
          force-avd-creation: false
          # A small userdata partition, so the AVD fits in what the runner has
          # left. The create step and the run step must agree, because they
          # share one cached AVD.
          disk-size: 2048M
          profile: pixel_6
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -camera-back none
          disable-animations: false
          script: echo "Device created and snapshotted for the cache."

      - name: Remove emulator locks before caching the device
        if: steps.avd-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: if [ -d ~/.android/avd ]; then find ~/.android/avd -name '*.lock' -type f -print -delete; fi

      - name: Save the device and its snapshot
        if: steps.avd-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.android/avd/*
            ~/.android/adb*
          key: android-avd-35-default-x86_64-disk2g-pixel6-clean

      # The runner's emulator is emulator-5554, where the Makefile expects
      # the local one at emulator-5556, so the serial is passed in.
      - name: Run the screen tests
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 35
          target: default
          arch: x86_64
          force-avd-creation: false
          # A small userdata partition, so the AVD fits in what the runner has
          # left. The create step and the run step must agree, because they
          # share one cached AVD.
          disk-size: 2048M
          profile: pixel_6
          emulator-options: -no-snapshot-save -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -camera-back none
          # The tests read what is on screen, and a view in the middle of an
          # animation is present but not yet where it will be.
          disable-animations: true
          script: make e2e ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554

      - name: Upload the test reports
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: e2e-test-reports
          path: |
            app/build/reports/androidTests/
            app/build/outputs/androidTest-results/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

name: Preview APK

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

# A newer push to the same pull request or to main makes the running build
# pointless, so it is cancelled.
concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# The token only checks out the repository. The cache and the artifact upload
# use the runner's own token, and the run summary needs no token at all.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # An APK for every pull request and every push to main, to install on a
  # phone straight from the run's summary page. It is the preview build type
  # from app/build.gradle.kts: a debug build named "EdgeVPN preview" under the
  # application id com.kairos.edgevpn.preview, so it sits next to a released
  # app instead of replacing it.
  preview-apk:
    name: Build preview APK
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # The runner has its own Android SDK and points ANDROID_HOME at it. The
      # Makefile would then use that SDK, which lacks the NDK version it
      # needs. Pointing it at binaries/ makes the Makefile install exactly
      # the SDK packages it lists, and the cache below keeps them.
      ANDROID_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/binaries/android-sdk
      # The key's name inside the keystore. It is not sensitive, and it is
      # kept out of the secrets on purpose: GitHub replaces every occurrence
      # of a secret's value in a job's logs with ***, and "edgevpn" appears in
      # package names, paths and the APK's name.
      EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS: edgevpn
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # A pull request's APK is named for its number, and one built from
      # main for its commit, so a download says which build it is.
      - name: Name the APK
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
            echo "APK_NAME=edgevpn-preview-pr$PR_NUMBER.apk" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo "APK_NAME=edgevpn-preview-main-${GITHUB_SHA::7}.apk" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: golib/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: golib/go.sum

      # The JDK, Android SDK and NDK, Gradle and gomobile that the Makefile
      # downloads into binaries/. They are about 1.5GB and the same bytes on
      # every run. The Makefile pins every version, and go.mod pins gomobile,
      # so a change to either one is a new cache.
      - name: Cache the build tools
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries
            !binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            !binaries/android-sdk/system-images
            !binaries/testpeer
          key: build-tools-${{ hashFiles('Makefile', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      # Signed with the release key so each preview installs over the one
      # before it. A pull request that gets no secrets, such as one opened by
      # Dependabot, has an empty value here, and the build falls back to the
      # runner's debug key; that APK installs only on a phone that has no
      # preview on it yet.
      - name: Write the keystore
        env:
          KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$KEYSTORE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$KEYSTORE_BASE64" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/release.keystore"
            echo "EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE=$RUNNER_TEMP/release.keystore" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo "No signing secret; the preview is signed with a debug key."
          fi

      - name: Build the preview APK
        env:
          EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          make preview
          mv app/build/outputs/apk/preview/app-preview.apk \
            "app/build/outputs/apk/preview/$APK_NAME"

      - name: Remove the keystore
        if: always()
        run: rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/release.keystore"

      # Uploaded as the bare APK rather than inside a zip, so a phone's
      # browser downloads something it can install.
      - name: Upload the APK
        id: upload
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          path: app/build/outputs/apk/preview/${{ env.APK_NAME }}
          archive: false
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Link the APK from the run summary
        env:
          ARTIFACT_ID: ${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-id }}
        run: |
          url="$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/artifacts/$ARTIFACT_ID"
          echo "Install on a phone: [$APK_NAME]($url)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

jobs:

      - name: Check the signing secrets are set
        env:

        run: |
          missing=""
          for name in EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_BASE64 EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              missing="$missing $name"
            fi
          done
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "Missing repository secret(s):$missing" >&2
            echo "See 'Signing' in README.md for how to set them." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: golib/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: golib/go.sum

      - name: Cache the build tools
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            binaries
            !binaries/android-sdk/emulator
            !binaries/android-sdk/system-images
            !binaries/testpeer
          key: build-tools-${{ hashFiles('Makefile', 'golib/go.mod') }}

      # versionName and versionCode come from this, in app/build.gradle.kts.
      # The leading v of the tag is not part of the version.
      - name: Read the version from the tag
        run: echo "EDGEVPN_VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Decoded into the runner's temp directory, never the checkout, and
      # removed once the build is done, whether or not it succeeded.
      - name: Write the keystore
        env:
          KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
        run: echo "$KEYSTORE_BASE64" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/release.keystore"

      - name: Build the signed release APK
        env:
          EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE: ${{ runner.temp }}/release.keystore
          EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          make release
          mv app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk \
            "app/build/outputs/apk/release/edgevpn-$GITHUB_REF_NAME.apk"

      - name: Remove the keystore
        if: always()
        run: rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/release.keystore"

      # Named for the tag, with the tag's own message as its notes. The
      # release may already exist: one made in the web interface creates the
      # tag that starts this run, and a re-run arrives after its own earlier
      # attempt made one. So an existing release gets the APK added, and
      # --clobber lets a re-run replace the APK it uploaded before.
      - name: Publish the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release view "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

              --notes-from-tag

# Network changes: design

Date: 2026-11-06. Epic: issue #1, step 7. Branch: `feat/network-changes`.

## What the user sees today

A phone runs the VPN on home Wi-Fi and the owner walks out of the house. Wi-Fi drops and the phone moves to mobile data. The app does nothing about it. The VPN comes back only when libp2p happens to notice that its connections are dead and something dials again, which can take minutes. Coming home again, the phone never starts local discovery (mDNS) on the Wi-Fi if the VPN was started on mobile data.

None of this has been measured on the phone yet (epic step 2). The test below measures it on the emulator first, before any fix, so the change is judged against a number.

## Goal

After the phone switches between Wi-Fi and mobile data, VPN traffic works again within 10 seconds, without the user doing anything. The emulator test checks a looser bound (see Testing) and logs the measured time.

## Non-goals

- A seamless handover. libp2p has no QUIC connection migration, and QUIC is off anyway (epic step 6). A switch interrupts traffic for a few seconds.
- Faster discovery through the public DHT (a separate epic item).
- Stopping mDNS from advertising the VPN and mobile data addresses on Wi-Fi (epic step 3). The new mDNS runner below makes that easier later, but it stays a separate change.
- Battery tuning (epic step 8). The keepalive change below has a battery cost that step 8 measures.

## How it works today

- Kotlin (`EdgeVpnService`) builds the VPN, takes a Wi-Fi multicast lock and starts Go. It never listens for network changes.
- Go dials through protected sockets (`VpnService.protect`), so the dials bypass the VPN and leave through whatever network Android uses at that moment.
- libp2p recomputes the phone's own addresses every 5 seconds. Our `androidAddrsFactory` reads the interfaces each time, so the advertised addresses already follow the network, and libp2p tells connected peers about new addresses through identify push.
- edgevpn runs the Android mDNS discovery once, at node start (`pkg/discovery/mdns_android.go`). It picks the multicast interfaces at that moment and never looks again. Started on mobile data, it finds no Wi-Fi interface and skips mDNS for the whole session.
- A dead connection is noticed by the yamux keepalive: a ping every 30 seconds with a 10 second timeout, so up to 40 seconds. When Android itself removes an interface's address it usually also destroys the TCP sockets on it, which closes those connections at once (expected from Android's design, untested here).
- After a failed dial, libp2p's swarm keeps the peer's addresses in a dial backoff for a while, so a redial right after a switch can be refused without trying.

## Design

### Kotlin: watch the network

A new class `UnderlyingNetworkWatcher` in the service owns two network callbacks for the session: one for the best network, one for the local flag. Both are registered in `connect()` after `Edgevpn.start` succeeds and unregistered in `teardown()`.

Which network to watch: an app's default network, as reported by `registerDefaultNetworkCallback`, is the VPN itself when the VPN applies to the app, and it does apply to this app. So the watcher asks for the best network that is not a VPN:

- Android 12 (API 31) and later: `registerBestMatchingNetworkCallback` with a request for `NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET` and `NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_VPN`. Android does the ranking.
- Android 8 to 11 (API 26 to 30): `registerNetworkCallback` with the same request, keeping the capabilities of every network it reports. A pure function picks the current one: validated before not validated, then Wi-Fi, then Ethernet, then cellular. This path is untested on a real device; the emulator image in CI is API 35.

The local flag comes from the second callback: `registerNetworkCallback` with a request for `NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_VPN` and the transports Wi-Fi or Ethernet, with `NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET` removed. `onLocalNetwork` is true while any network it reports is connected, whatever its internet or validation state. The best network alone would be the wrong source: on a Wi-Fi with only a LAN, Android ranks validated cellular first, and mDNS would stop although its peers are on that Wi-Fi. A pure function, `onLocalNetwork`, makes the decision and has unit tests. The flag is false on mobile data alone and when no network is left.

When the best network or the local flag changes, the watcher:

1. calls `setUnderlyingNetworks(arrayOf(network))` with the best network, or `setUnderlyingNetworks(null)` when no network with internet is left. The VPN carries only 10.1.0.0/24, so this does not change routing; it makes Android report the right transport and metered state for the VPN to other apps and in Settings.
2. calls `Edgevpn.networkChanged(onLocalNetwork)`.

The first report after registering also goes through both steps, so Go learns the starting network type.

The multicast lock stays as it is: taken at start, released at teardown. A lock taken through `WifiManager` is expected to survive Wi-Fi going away and coming back, but that is untested. The emulator test checks only that mDNS starts again on `wlan0` after Wi-Fi returns. It cannot check that mDNS finds the peer, because the test peer sits behind the emulator's NAT and no multicast reaches it. If a phone shows that mDNS finds nothing after Wi-Fi returns, the watcher should also release and take the lock again on each change.

### Go: `NetworkChanged(onLocalNetwork bool)`

A new exported function. It returns at once; the work runs on its own goroutine, so the Kotlin callback thread never waits on network I/O. When the VPN is not running it does nothing.

Bursts of callbacks (Android often reports a change in several steps) are merged: the work runs 500 ms after the last call, with the `onLocalNetwork` value of the last call. A call that arrives while the work is running schedules one more run after it.

The work, in order:

1. **Close connections on gone addresses.** Read the current interface addresses with `anet.InterfaceAddrs()`. Close every connection whose local address has an IP that is not among them. Connections whose local address has no IP component are left alone. The decision is a pure function, `staleConns(localIPs []net.IP, conns []connAddr) []int`, with unit tests.
2. **Restart mDNS.** Stop the running mDNS discovery. When `onLocalNetwork` is true, start it again, so it picks the interfaces that exist now. On mobile data mDNS stays off, since there is no local network to find peers on.
3. **Redial.** Dial, in parallel and with a 10 second timeout each, the bootstrap peers from the token and every peer that owns an entry in the machines bucket of the ledger. Before each dial the swarm's dial backoff for that peer is cleared (`Backoff().Clear`, `p2p/net/swarm/swarm_dial.go`), so a dial that failed on the old network does not block the new one. `network.WithForceDirectDial` also skips the backoff, but it drops relay addresses, and on mobile data a relay may be the only way to reach a peer. Peers already connected through a connection that survived step 1 are skipped.

Nothing extra is needed for the advertised addresses: libp2p recomputes them within 5 seconds, as described above. AutoRelay books a new relay slot by itself when its reservation's connection closes. The DHT routing table is left alone; edgevpn keeps its DHT object private, and kad-dht reconnects to more peers by itself when its table runs low (untested).

### Go: mDNS that can be restarted

edgevpn starts mDNS once with the node's context. To restart it, the app turns edgevpn's mDNS off in `networkConfig` (`Discovery.MDNS: false`) and runs the same upstream discovery itself:

- A network service, added next to `hostReadyService`, starts `(&discovery.MDNS{DiscoveryServiceTag: tag}).Run(logger, childCtx, host)` with a context derived from the node's context.
- `tag` is the `mdns` field of the token, decoded the same way as in `ValidateToken`. It is a secret, so it never goes to the log; the existing scrubbing of the mDNS start line in `logbuffer.go` keeps working because the upstream code logs the same line.
- A restart cancels `childCtx`, which shuts down the zeroconf server and the browse loop, and calls `Run` again with a new child context.
- The service starts mDNS only after Kotlin's first report says the phone is on a local network, so a session started on mobile data does not advertise on the mobile interface.

Unit tests use a fake run function to check: no start before a local network is reported, one stop and one start per restart, nothing left running after Stop.

### Go: notice silent drops faster

A connection can also die without any network change, for example when a NAT forgets the mapping. The app replaces libp2p's default muxer with yamux configured for a 10 second keepalive interval and a 5 second ping timeout (`libp2p.Muxer(yamux.ID, ...)`). edgevpn adds its default muxers only when none are set (`pkg/node/connection.go`), so this one wins. A silent drop is then noticed in at most 15 seconds instead of 40.

The cost is one small ping per connection every 10 seconds, also over mobile data with the screen off. The phone keeps a few dozen connections (DHT peers, relays, VPN peers), so step 8 measures what this does to the battery and may raise the interval.

## Testing

Test first, as everywhere in this repository.

Go unit tests (`make test`):

- `staleConns` for IPv4 and IPv6, for a gone address, for a kept address and for an address without an IP.
- The debounce: several calls within 500 ms run the work once, with the last value; a call during a run gives exactly one more run. A fake clock or a short test interval keeps the tests fast.
- `NetworkChanged` before Start and after Stop does nothing.
- The mDNS runner with a fake run function, as listed above.
- `networkConfig` turns edgevpn's mDNS off, and the muxer option carries the keepalive values.

Kotlin unit test: the pure function that picks the network on API 26 to 30.

Emulator test, a new part of `scripts/network-test` (and so of `make network-test` and the CI network job). The emulator has Wi-Fi (`wlan0`) and mobile data (`eth0`, shown as LTE), and both reach the QEMU test peer through the emulator's NAT:

1. Connect as today and wait until pings work both ways.
2. Run a ping from the peer to the app in the background, then `svc wifi disable`. Measure the time until pings work both ways again over mobile data.
3. `svc wifi enable`. Measure again, and check in the log that mDNS started again on `wlan0`. Before this step, check that no fresh mDNS start was logged while only mobile data was left.
4. Airplane mode on (`cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable`) for 10 seconds, then off. Measure again.

Each step fails above 60 seconds and logs the measured time. 60 seconds is looser than the 10 second goal because CI emulators are slow and the bound must not flake; the measured times on a local run go into the pull request. Before the fix, the same steps run once on `main` to record the baseline, which is the RED for this test.

A test of a Wi-Fi network without internet needs a second Wi-Fi network on the emulator, which it does not have. It stays for the phone.

## Decisions

Approved by the owner on 2026-11-06, with these answers:

- The keepalive starts at 10 seconds; step 8 tunes it with battery measurements.
- No mDNS on mobile data, tethered setups included.

# Status screen, settings and logs: design

Date: 2026-11-05. Approved mockups: `2026-11-05-status-screen/main-screen.html`, `2026-11-05-status-screen/settings.html` and `2026-11-05-status-screen/help-icons.html` (open them in a browser; they are self-contained HTML fragments, so unstyled bits are expected).

## Why

Today the app shows one line, "Status: connected", a Disconnect button, and a log panel that is empty until it is opened. "Connected" is set before anything has connected and stays even when the node has failed. The only way to know whether the phone reaches the other devices is to read logs on the phone or run the edgevpn API on a desktop.

The owner wants to see on the phone itself which devices of their network are reachable and whether each one is reached directly or through a relay, as a debugging aid that replaces log reading for most questions. The screen must make sense to someone who does not know VPN or EdgeVPN terms.

## Goals

- One main screen that answers: is the VPN working, which of my devices can I reach right now, and how.
- Plain language on every screen except the logs. Words to use: "network key" (token), "address in your network" (VPN IP), "direct" and "helper only" (direct and relayed connection; no VPN traffic flows over a relayed one), "public helpers" (other libp2p peers on the internet), "phone ID" (libp2p peer ID).
- A truthful status: "connected" only when at least one device is reachable.
- Logs that exist whether or not a screen was open when they were written.

## Non-goals

- Managing other devices (removing them from the network, renaming them).
- Bandwidth graphs or traffic counters.
- Automatic address assignment (edgevpn DHCP). The phone's VPN address must be known before Android's `VpnService.Builder.establish()`, and DHCP assigns it after the node joins, so it needs a reconnect dance. Later.
- The IPv6 and mDNS issues listed in issue #1.

## Anti-goals

- Peer IDs, multiaddrs, "DHT", "ledger", "relay circuit" or "libp2p" on the main screen or in settings labels. They belong in the logs and in the copyable phone ID only.
- Any badge or status that claims more than the code knows. If a fact is unknown (for example "last seen" for a device that never checked in), leave it out instead of guessing.

## Constraints

- Existing stack: Kotlin with Android Views and Material Components (`com.google.android.material:material:1.11.0`), minSdk 26, targetSdk 34, Go library bound with gomobile. Stay on Views; no Jetpack Compose (listed under the calls at the end).
- gomobile can only pass basic types between Go and Kotlin (int, string, bool, []byte, interfaces with such methods). A `[]byte` passed from Kotlin is only valid during the call; Go must copy it if it keeps it.
- Everything runs on one phone with arm64 only (`-target android/arm64`).
- Code is written test first (Go `testing`, Kotlin JUnit 4 already set up under `app/src/test`).

## Screens

### Main screen

Top to bottom, as in the "Connected" mockup:

1. **Status card**, coloured by state:
   - **Off** (grey): VPN service not running. "VPN is off", one sentence on what that means, button "Turn on".
   - **Looking for your devices** (orange): node running, zero devices reachable. Shows how long ago it started and that this can take a few minutes on mobile data.
   - **Connected** (green): node running, at least one device reachable. "You can reach N of your M devices."
   - **Problem** (red, not in the mockups; same layout): the VPN could not start or stopped with an error. Shows a plain sentence plus "See logs", and the button "Try again". The raw error goes to the logs. Covers every failure, not only background ones: Go's `Start` returning an error (bad key, config error), `establish()` returning null, the node key failing to load, and `node.Start` returning an error later. In all of them the VPN is torn down completely (tunnel closed, foreground notification removed, service stopped), and the reason is remembered so the screen can show it. "Try again" starts the VPN like "Turn on". The Problem state lasts until the next start attempt or "Turn off".
   - In every state except Off: two pills, "This phone" with its address in the network, and "Using" with `Wi-Fi` or `Mobile data` (from `ConnectivityManager` network capabilities of the active underlying network). The mockup shows the Wi-Fi name; reading it needs the location permission, so it is left out (design call, see the end).
   - Button "Turn off" / "Turn on" in the card.
2. **Map**: the phone in the centre, each device of the network around it. Line style per device: solid green for direct, dashed orange for helper only, faint dotted grey for offline. Device icon plus its name under it. Up to 8 devices placed evenly on a circle; beyond 8, show 7 and a "+N more" bubble. Hidden in the Off state; in the Looking state it shows only the phone with a pulsing ring. Drawn with a custom `View` on a `Canvas`.
3. **Your devices**: one row per device, sorted direct first, then helper only, then offline, then by name. Row: icon, name, second line "`<address in network>` · `<how>`", badge on the right.
   - `<how>`: "same Wi-Fi as you" (direct, and the remote IP is a private address in the same subnet as one of the phone's Wi-Fi addresses), "over the internet" (direct otherwise), "found through a helper, no traffic yet" (helper only), "last seen X ago" (offline, when a check-in time is known), "not reachable right now" (offline, no check-in time).
   - Badge: "Direct", "Helper only", "Offline".
   - Name: the device's announced hostname. When it is empty or "localhost" (what Android devices announce), show "Unnamed device" instead.
   - Tapping a row opens a small details sheet: name, address in network, how it is reached, the remote address the phone is connected to (as plain IP and port, not multiaddr), phone ID of that device with copy. This sheet is the one place where a technical value appears outside the logs.
4. **Finding your devices**: two tiles. "N public helpers available": the number of peers the phone currently has open connections to that are not devices of the network. "X ago, last heard from your network": the newest check-in time from any other device.
5. Overflow menu (⋮): Settings, Logs.

The screen refreshes every 2 seconds while visible, and stops refreshing when not visible.

### Settings

As in the "Joined a network" mockup:

- **Network card**: "You're part of a network", a sentence about keeping the key private, buttons "Replace key" (opens the Join screen) and "Leave network" (confirmation dialog, then disconnects and deletes the stored network key). The phone's identity key (`NodeKeyStore`) is kept, so if the phone joins the same network again it is the same device to the others and does not leave a second, locked entry behind. The dialog says: "This phone will disconnect and forget the network key. You can join again later with the key." The key is never displayed.
- **This phone**:
  - **Name**: what other devices see in their device lists. Defaults to the phone's model name (`Build.MODEL`, for example "Pixel 8"). Changing it takes effect while connected, without a reconnect.
  - **Address in your network**: an IPv4 address, default `10.1.0.2`. Validated as a dotted IPv4 address. Changing it while connected asks to reconnect. It replaces the hardcoded `10.1.0.2` in both `EdgeVpnService.kt` (`Builder.addAddress`) and `golib/edgevpn.go` (`Address`). The route stays `10.1.0.0/24` derived from the address with a /24 mask.
- **Troubleshooting**:
  - **View logs**: opens the Logs screen.
  - **Detailed logs** switch, off by default. Off: app log level info, libp2p log level error. On: both debug. Applies immediately to a running node and is remembered.
  - **Phone ID**: the libp2p peer ID, shortened in the middle, tap to copy the full value.
  - **Start fresh** (red text): deletes everything the app has stored, which is the network key, the phone's identity key, the name, the address, the detailed-logs choice and the log buffer, after disconnecting. Confirmation dialog: "This phone will forget the network and become a new device. Your other devices may show the old phone as a separate, unreachable device for a few minutes. You'll need the network key to join again." After it, the app shows the Join screen.
- **About**: app version name, and the edgevpn version the library was built with (from Go's `debug.ReadBuildInfo`).

### Join a network

Shown from the main screen when no key is stored, and from "Replace key". As in the "First time" mockup:

- Multi-line paste field, a sentence saying where the key comes from (the same token the user's computer uses to run EdgeVPN), "Join network" button.
- Validation before saving: the key, with whitespace removed, must decode as base64 to an edgevpn config that has the fields a node needs to start (the Go side decides this: add an exported `ValidateToken(token string) string` that returns an empty string when valid and a short plain-language reason otherwise). Shown under the field: "This doesn't look like a complete key. It may have been cut off while copying."
- "Scan QR code instead": scans a QR code containing the token. Uses `com.journeyapps:zxing-android-embedded` (works without Google Play services, which matters on LineageOS). Needs the camera permission, asked at the moment of scanning.

### Logs

A full screen with the most recent log lines, newest at the bottom, auto-scrolling unless the user has scrolled up, and a "Copy all" action. Lines are kept by the Go library in a ring buffer of the last 2000 lines, so they exist even when no screen was open. The Go library also writes every line to logcat itself (tag `EdgeVPN`), so `make logs` works regardless of what the UI is doing.

The buffer and the Logs screen hold edgevpn's own messages (the ones that go through `bufferLogger`), not libp2p's. libp2p logs through its own logging package to standard error, which gomobile forwards to logcat under the tag `GoLog` (seen on the phone). At debug level libp2p writes thousands of lines a minute and would push edgevpn's lines out of the buffer within seconds. So "Detailed logs" makes edgevpn's messages in the buffer more detailed (debug instead of info) and raises libp2p to debug in logcat only. The Logs screen says so in one line at the top when detailed logs are on: "Network library details are in the developer log (logcat)."

### Help: the (?) icons

Every plain-language term gets a small, faded (?) icon next to it, the first time the term appears on a screen: the status title, the "This phone" and "Using" pills, section titles, each badge, each tile, the map legend, and each settings item. Placement rule: the icon sits directly after the last word of its term, vertically centred on that line of text, and scales with the text size (about the height of a capital letter, never under 13 dp of visible circle; the touch target is at least 48 dp, extended around the icon). When a label wraps, the icon stays attached to its last word and never wraps onto a line of its own or drifts to the edge of its container. In Android, put the icon inline in the text (an image span or a compound drawable), not as a separate view aligned to the container. The mockup shows the intended result.

Tapping it opens a bottom sheet with:

## Go library changes

- **Check-ins**: add edgevpn's `services.Alive(120s, 600s, 900s)` to the node options, the same as the CLI does for VPN nodes (`cmd/main.go`). Without it other devices show the phone as offline, and the phone has no "last seen" data for them. Extend the existing CLI-defaults test.
- **Snapshot**: an exported `Snapshot() string` returning JSON, read by the app every 2 seconds. Contents:
  - `state`: `off`, `looking`, `connected`, `problem`, plus `startedAt` and, for `problem`, `error` and, when there is a raw error that cannot contain the network key, `detail`.
  - `self`: phone ID, address in network.
  - `devices`: for each entry of the ledger's machines bucket other than this phone: name (`Hostname`), address (`Address`), phone ID (`PeerID`), `reach` (`direct`, `helper`, `offline`), `remote` (IP and port of the best open connection, if any), `sameNetwork` (bool, per the rule above, computed in Go from the phone's interface addresses via `anet`), `lastSeen` (from the HealthCheck bucket, omitted if unknown).
  - `helpers`: count of connected peers that are not devices.
  - `lastHeard`: newest HealthCheck time from another device, omitted if none.
  - `addressInUse`: true while this node rejected another peer's machines entry for the phone's own address less than 60 seconds ago, omitted otherwise. golib reads the rejection from the arguments of edgevpn's "ownership violation (rejected)" warning, which the ledger passes to the node logger, and counts only the reason "overwrite of a live entry owned by another peer" (a rejected deletion, which a device receives when it comes back after the other side dropped its entry, is no clash); the phone's own copy of the ledger always holds its own entry, so the ledger contents cannot show the clash. The record is cleared on Start and Stop. The status card then says "Another device already uses 10.1.0.2. Pick another address in Settings." with a (?) and a "Change address" button that opens Settings.
- **Reach rule**: look at `Host().Network().ConnsToPeer(id)`. Any connection that is not limited (`Stat().Limited == false`) and whose remote multiaddr has no `/p2p-circuit` component: `direct`. Else, any connection at all: `helper`. Else: `offline`. Keep this a pure function over a small description of the connections so it can be unit tested without a network.
- **State rule**: `off` when no node runs and no failure is remembered, `problem` when the last start attempt failed at any stage (see the Problem state), `connected` when at least one device is `direct` or `helper`, otherwise `looking`. A failure is remembered until the next `Start` or `Stop`. The Kotlin side reports its own start failures (establish, key loading) to Go with an exported `ReportStartFailure(reason string)` so there is one source of truth. When `node.Start` fails in the background, Go closes the tunnel and notifies the service through a callback interface so it can stop itself. `Status()` follows the same rule.
- **Logs**: the ring buffer described above, an exported `RecentLogs() string`, logcat writing from Go, and `SetDetailedLogs(on bool)` which changes both the app log level and the libp2p log level at runtime.
- **Settings inputs**: `Start` gains the address and the name (strings), and `SetName(name string)` changes the name while running.
- **Name announcement**: edgevpn's VPN service announces the phone with `os.Hostname()`, which Android reports as "localhost", and has no option to change it. It only rewrites the phone's entry in the machines bucket when the entry is missing or has another peer ID (`pkg/vpn/vpn.go:109` in v0.35.5). The library runs its own announcement on the same interval (`Ledger.Announce`, 10 s): when the phone's entry under its address has this phone's peer ID and a different hostname, it writes the same entry with the chosen hostname, signed like every other write. edgevpn's loop then leaves it alone. A Go test pins this: it runs edgevpn's announce condition against an entry written by the library and fails if edgevpn would overwrite it, so a future edgevpn release that compares more fields is caught at upgrade time instead of as two writers fighting on the network. If no such test is possible without a running network, the builder writes the closest test that exercises the library's write and checks the code path manually on upgrade (note this in the plan).
- **Versions**: `LibraryVersion() string` with the edgevpn module version.

# EdgeVPN Android

An Android app that joins a phone to an [EdgeVPN](https://github.com/mudler/edgevpn) network. EdgeVPN is a peer-to-peer VPN built on [libp2p](https://libp2p.io): the devices in a network find each other through local discovery (mDNS) and a public internet-wide directory (the libp2p DHT), and send their traffic to each other directly, with no central server. Every device in a network shares one network key, a base64 string that `edgevpn -g -b` generates.

With the app, a phone gets an address in the VPN, shows the other devices of the network and whether it can reach them, and reconnects by itself when it moves between Wi-Fi and mobile data. Android 8 (API 26) or newer is needed.

The app is young. It works on Wi-Fi and on mobile data, but a switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data can interrupt the VPN for a few minutes; see [Current status](#current-status) and [Known limitations](#known-limitations).

## Install

Download the APK of the latest [release](https://github.com/jimmykarily/edgevpn-android/releases) on the phone and open it. Android asks once to allow installs from the browser. Then open the app, paste the network key on the Join screen or scan it as a QR code, and turn the VPN on. The phone uses the VPN address `10.1.0.2` unless another one is set in Settings; every device in a network needs its own address.

## How it works

The VPN itself is edgevpn's Go code, compiled into the app with `gomobile bind`. The Kotlin side runs an Android `VpnService`: it creates the tunnel, hands its file descriptor to Go, and shows the state. The Go side (`golib/`) starts an edgevpn node, keeps the app's own libp2p sockets outside the tunnel with `VpnService.protect`, and reports the network's devices back to the app. [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) has more detail, and `docs/superpowers/` holds the design notes of larger changes.

## Test peer

Real-network checks need a second device in the network. `scripts/testpeer` runs one: a disposable QEMU VM (Debian 12 cloud image, KVM, 512 MB, headless) with edgevpn inside, at VPN address `10.1.0.10`. It needs `qemu-system-x86_64`, `qemu-img`, `xorriso`, `ssh` and a usable `/dev/kvm`, and no root: the VM uses QEMU user-mode networking.

| Target | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `make peer-up` | Start the VM with a new temporary network key and wait until edgevpn is up |
| `make peer-down` | Stop the VM and delete the run directory, including the key |
| `make peer-status` | Whether the VM and edgevpn are running, and the VPN interface |

`scripts/testpeer` also has `ping <addr>` (ping from inside the VM), `logs` (the VM's edgevpn log), `serial` (its console log), `scrub` (stdin to stdout without the key), `key` (the path of the key file, never its contents), `addr` (the VM's libp2p address as the emulator reaches it) and `readdress <addr>` (restart edgevpn in the VM with another VPN address).

The first `up` downloads the cloud image and builds edgevpn at the version `golib/go.mod` requires, both into `binaries/testpeer/`. Each run boots from a fresh overlay disk and generates its own key into `binaries/testpeer/run/token`; the owner's network key is never used. edgevpn in the VM runs with an ownership TTL of 60 seconds instead of the default 8 minutes, so it forgets a device that has been silent for about a minute. The host forwards `127.0.0.1:40022` to the VM's SSH and `127.0.0.1:40001` to its libp2p port (override with `TESTPEER_SSH_PORT` and `TESTPEER_P2P_PORT`).

## Network test

`make network-test` checks the app on a real network: the debug app on the emulator joins the test peer's network, the VPN network has no unreachable IPv6 route (which would block IPv6 for every app), both sides ping each other, and the VPN is turned off for 90 seconds (longer than the peer's ownership TTL, so the peer drops the app from its machine list) and on again, after which pings must work again and the app must still have exactly two listening sockets. With Android's "Always-on VPN, block connections without VPN" IPv6 may now bypass the VPN; that is acceptable because the VPN carries only 10.1.0.0/24, and it is untested. The off and on part guards against an old libp2p host staying alive after the VPN stops.

```bash
make emu-up         # start the emulator, once
make network-test   # build, start the peer if needed, run the check
```

The script, `scripts/network-test`, stores the peer's temporary key, the address `10.1.0.4` and the peer's libp2p address in the app through an instrumented helper (`NetworkTestSetup`), grants the VPN permission with `appops`, and drives the main screen through `adb`. The app dials the peer directly at `10.0.2.2` (the host as the emulator sees it) instead of looking for it through the public DHT, so it connects in seconds. Because the peer forgets a device after 60 seconds without a heartbeat, the test also makes the app send one every 15 seconds instead of every 120. Neither setting has a screen in the app.

It writes screenshots, the app's log and the peer's edgevpn and console logs into `build/network-test/`. Every log it shows or writes (not the screenshots) goes through `scripts/scrub-key` first, which removes the key, the secrets inside it and any 12-character piece of either, and which prints nothing if it has no key to scrub with (`make test` runs its self-test). Screenshots are not scrubbed. They show only the app's screens for this run's throwaway key, and the Join screen, the one screen a key can be typed into, blocks screenshots. It clears the app's data at the end so the key does not stay on the device. A peer it started is stopped again. `NETWORK_TEST_LONG=0` skips the off/on part for a quick local run; CI always runs it. Before that part, the script switches the emulator's network: Wi-Fi off, Wi-Fi on, and airplane mode on for 10 seconds then off. Android 8 has no `cmd connectivity airplane-mode`, so there the script restarts adbd as root to send the airplane mode broadcast, and back to non-root at the end; this needs an image that allows `adb root`, such as the `default` images. The script has run on Android 8 (API 26), 11 (API 30) and 15 (API 35) emulators. After each step both sides must ping each other again, and the script logs `switch <step>: <n>s`. A step fails above `NETWORK_TEST_SWITCH_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 60), and `NETWORK_TEST_SWITCH=0` skips these steps. The script also checks the app's mDNS, the local discovery that finds peers on the same Wi-Fi: while Wi-Fi is off and only mobile data is left, no fresh `mdns(android): using interfaces:` log line may appear, and after Wi-Fi is back a fresh one must list `wlan0` and nothing else. No such line in the whole run may list `eth0`, which is mobile data on the emulator. These checks run by default; `NETWORK_TEST_MDNS_CHECK=0` skips them. Wi-Fi is switched on and airplane mode off again when the script ends, also after a failure.

The test also guards the app's calls to `VpnService.protect`, which keeps the app's own sockets out of the VPN. They run on the dialing thread. In the network test runs protect never failed off the main thread on an API 35 emulator; vendor phone builds are untested. The script enlarges the emulator's log buffer and fails if the app logged `VpnService.protect(...) returned false`, once after the first connect and once at the end. That log line is also the sign to look for on a real phone.

`make network-test-address-in-use` uses the same setup and then checks the warning about a shared address. Before the app turns on, the peer moves to the app's address `10.1.0.4` (`scripts/testpeer readdress`, which restarts edgevpn in the VM and so empties its ledger) and waits until it lists itself there. The app, turned on afterwards, must show "Another device already uses 10.1.0.4. Pick another address in Settings." while still looking for devices, and its "Change address" button must open Settings. The peer gets `10.1.0.10` back at the end when the test did not start it. Its files go into `build/network-test/address-in-use/`.

The **Network tests** workflow (`.github/workflows/network.yml`) runs `make network-test` and then `make network-test-address-in-use` on every pull request and every push to `main`, and uploads `build/network-test/` when it fails. It uses no secrets.

## APKs from CI

Two GitHub Actions workflows build APKs that install on a phone:

- **Preview** (`.github/workflows/preview.yml`) runs on every pull request and every push to `main`. The run's summary page has an "Install on a phone" link to the APK, which a phone's browser can download and install directly. The preview is a debug build, but not debuggable, named "EdgeVPN preview" with the application id `com.kairos.edgevpn.preview`, so it installs next to a released app instead of replacing it. Previews are kept for 14 days.
- **Release** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) runs when a tag starting with `v` is pushed, for example `v0.2.0`. It builds a release APK whose version comes from the tag (`0.2.0`, version code `200`), and attaches it to a GitHub release named after the tag, using the tag's message as release notes. Each part of the version must be under 100.

```bash
git tag -a v0.2.0 -m "What changed in this release"
git push origin v0.2.0
```

Both workflows run the same `make` targets as a local build, and cache `binaries/` between runs.

## Signing

Android only installs an update over an installed app when both are signed with the same key. Every CI build is signed with one release key, so each preview installs over the previous preview, and each release over the previous release.

The key is a PKCS12 keystore with one RSA 4096 key under the alias `edgevpn`. It was generated on 2026-11-05 and is valid for 10000 days. Its certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint is:

```
F0:31:8D:E9:12:35:C1:72:1E:58:DB:2C:61:A6:56:AC:1D:04:1A:55:21:4A:5B:7B:A3:D0:A6:9B:A0:12:31:30
```

The original copy lives outside the repository, in `~/.local/share/edgevpn-android/signing/` on the machine it was generated on:

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `release.keystore` | The keystore |
| `keystore-password` | The password of both the keystore and the key (PKCS12 uses one password for both) |
| `key-alias` | `edgevpn` |

**Back this directory up somewhere safe.** If the key is lost, a new key cannot produce updates for installed apps: every phone has to uninstall the app, losing its settings, before installing a build signed with a new key.

CI reads the key from these repository secrets (Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions):

| Secret | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_BASE64` | `release.keystore`, base64 encoded |
| `EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` | Contents of `keystore-password` |
| `EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Contents of `keystore-password` |

The alias is set in the workflows as a plain value rather than a secret. GitHub replaces every occurrence of a secret's value in the logs with `***`, and `edgevpn` appears in package names, paths and APK names.

To set the secrets again, for example after moving the key to a new machine, without printing any value:

```bash
D=~/.local/share/edgevpn-android/signing
R=jimmykarily/edgevpn-android
base64 -w0 "$D/release.keystore" | gh secret set EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_BASE64 -R $R
gh secret set EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD -R $R < "$D/keystore-password"
gh secret set EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD -R $R < "$D/keystore-password"
```

A pull request that gets no secrets, such as one from Dependabot, still builds a preview, signed with the runner's debug key. That APK only installs on a phone that has no preview installed yet. The release workflow refuses to run without the secrets.

To build a signed APK locally, set the same values as environment variables:

```bash
D=~/.local/share/edgevpn-android/signing
export EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE=$D/release.keystore
export EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS=edgevpn
export EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD="$(cat $D/keystore-password)"
export EDGEVPN_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD="$(cat $D/keystore-password)"
EDGEVPN_VERSION=0.2.0 make release
```

Without these variables, `make preview` signs with the local debug key and `make release` produces an unsigned APK.

## Current status

The phone joins an EdgeVPN network, appears in the web UI and routes traffic over Wi-Fi and over mobile data. On mobile data it reached a desktop at home directly over IPv6, because that carrier lets incoming IPv6 reach the phone. This was checked on one phone with one carrier. On a carrier that blocks incoming connections, the phone depends on relays and hole punching, which is untested on a real phone. Faster recovery after a network switch is tracked in [issue #1](https://github.com/jimmykarily/edgevpn-android/issues/1).

## Known limitations

- **A switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data interrupts the VPN for minutes.** When the phone leaves Wi-Fi, VPN traffic stopped for about 4 minutes (237 seconds, one run on one phone) before it came back on mobile data by itself. The phone redialled within seconds, but the home router blocked incoming connections to the desktop, so the phone reached it only through a relay, which carries no VPN traffic. The direct connection came back when the desktop dialled the phone's new address, most likely after its next search of the public directory (every 3 minutes). Shortening this is tracked in [issue #1](https://github.com/jimmykarily/edgevpn-android/issues/1).
- **No local discovery over the phone's own hotspot.** mDNS, the local discovery that finds devices on the same Wi-Fi, runs only on Wi-Fi and Ethernet networks the phone has joined. A laptop connected to the phone's hotspot is not found that way. It can still find the phone through the internet, like a device anywhere else, but that search is slower: about 5 minutes in our tests. The reason is that Android gives apps no public way to learn whether the hotspot is on or which network interface it uses (the tethering API is for system apps only). Without that, the app cannot tell the hotspot apart from mobile data, and mDNS stays off mobile data on purpose: no device there is meant to be reached, and on some devices, such as the emulator, mobile data does carry multicast.
